one_line: A mutilated sepoy and the humble Pune potter-surgeon whose preserved Indian rhinoplasty reshaped modern nose reconstruction.

appearance.age_look: Cowasjee appears as a lean Parsi man in his early 30s; the Pune surgeon appears as a wiry Deccan artisan in his late 30s.
appearance.face: Cowasjee has an oval face, light brown complexion, sharp nose now clearly reconstructed, neatly trimmed black moustache, thick brows and a calm, slightly wary gaze; the surgeon has a narrower face, medium-brown Deccan complexion, pointed nose, thin moustache and stubble, with focused, observant eyes and a composed, serious default expression.
appearance.hair: Cowasjee’s black hair is mostly hidden under a white Parsi-style rounded turban-cap (pugree) wrapped smoothly, with a small tail tuck at the back; what shows is short and neatly combed; the Pune surgeon’s black hair is tied back in a small low knot, partly covered by a simple dark indigo cotton headscarf band wrapped around his head like a narrow turban strip, leaving his forehead clear.
appearance.costume: Cowasjee wears a late-18th-century Parsi mercantile outfit: a long, straight-cut, calf-length white cotton jama (robe) with side-ties and slightly flared skirt, worn over a pale cream angarkha-style under-tunic, narrow off-white churidar trousers gathered at the ankles, and simple brown leather shoes; a light, soft grey woollen shawl is draped around his shoulders and forearms, and a narrow red sash is tied discreetly at his waist; the Pune surgeon wears a practical Maratha-region artisan dress: a knee-length, dull-ochre cotton angarkha tied diagonally across the chest with cloth ties, sleeves rolled just below the elbow, over plain dark-cream cotton dhoti folded and wrapped to mid-calf, with the pleats brought between the legs and tucked at the waist; he is barefoot, with a narrow, faded red cotton waistband, and a simple, earth-toned cotton shoulder cloth (light brown with a subtle thin darker border) looped from his left shoulder and hanging behind him, ready to be used as a working cloth; both men wear minimal jewellery: Cowasjee has a thin silver ring on one hand, while the surgeon wears a single small copper bangle on his right wrist.
appearance.signature: The shared signature prop is a compact 18th-century Indian surgical kit: a rolled dark-brown leather pouch tied with a red cord, which, when partially open in drawings, shows a few slender iron instruments such as a small straight knife, a narrow spatula, and a flat metallic plate; Cowasjee often holds the closed roll respectfully in both hands, while the surgeon is shown with the roll at his waist, tucked into his sash, or unrolled on a low wooden plank beside him.

ref_desc: Cowasjee is a lean early-30s Parsi man in a white jama, cream churidar, soft grey shawl, white turban-cap and brown shoes, beside a wiry late-30s Pune potter-surgeon in ochre angarkha, cream dhoti, indigo headscarf and shoulder cloth, both with a brown leather surgical-kit roll tied with red cord.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet showing two consistent figures together: first, Cowasjee, a lean Parsi man in his early 30s with light-brown skin, oval face, reconstructed nose, neat black moustache and calm eyes, wearing a smooth white rounded turban-cap, a long white straight-cut jama over a pale cream under-tunic, off-white churidar trousers gathered at the ankles, simple brown leather shoes, a narrow red sash at the waist and a soft grey shawl around his shoulders; second, the Pune surgeon, a wiry late-30s Deccan artisan with medium-brown skin, narrow face, thin moustache and stubble, intense focused eyes and serious expression, hair tied in a small knot under a dark indigo headscarf band, wearing a dull-ochre cotton angarkha tied diagonally across the chest with sleeves rolled just below the elbows, a dark-cream dhoti wrapped to mid-calf, barefoot, a faded red waistband and a light brown shoulder cloth with a slightly darker border looped from his left shoulder; show their shared signature prop clearly as a compact dark-brown leather surgical kit, rolled and tied with a red cord, in some views closed in Cowasjee’s hands and in others at the surgeon’s waist or partly unrolled with a few slender iron instruments and a flat metallic plate visible; arrange front, side and three-quarter views to emphasise consistent face shapes, hairstyles, garments and the limited palette of white, cream, ochre, indigo and soft grey, in a clean shonen-anime line style with no text.
